_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: Patients with an ultra-rare fusion-driven sarcoma (EMC) are eligible for recruiting trials that a condition search on their own diagnosis never returns, because eligibility is written on the molecular lesion while the registry's listed-conditions field is written on the histology; and the obvious fix, a keyword map, is worse than no map because two adjudicated trials that refuse the disease would both have passed a keyword screen.

blockers.summary: ARITH-B1 — the adjudication denominator: §3 prints 'four records adjudicated' against a numerator of THREE admitting records, and §5 prints the same 'four' against a numerator of TWO. Same quantity, two values, and neither matches the artifacts.
blockers.evidence: §3 (lines 138-142): 'Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits and offers enrolment in an observational cohort. Those are counts of the four records adjudicated here, not of the registry.' §5 (line 212): 'Four candidates were adjudicated: two admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse.' The artifacts: research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> "summary": {"candidates_adjudicated": 4, "admits_and_is_interventional": 1, "admits_but_is_observational": 1, "refused": 2}, and its "adjudications" list is exactly [NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101, NCT07188532]. Of THOSE four, exactly ONE admits and offers treatment, not two. The paper's second treating admitter, NCT05918640, is not in that file at all: it is research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.confirmed_fusion_family_defined, a one-element list ({"nct_id": "NCT05918640", "eligibility_text_retrieved": true, "eligibility_basis": "fusion-family-defined (FET: EWSR1 / FUS / TAF15)"}). So §3's numerator (3 admitting: NCT05918640, NCT06571734, NCT04151342) is drawn from a set of FIVE adjudicated records while its denominator is a batch of four that excludes one of them and includes two refusals discussed in §4. The alternative reading — 'here' = §3's own four table rows — is refuted by the paper's own §2: 'The basket records in §3's third row are the exception and are not adjudicated', and that row is nine records, not one. The sentence is therefore wrong under every reading, and it contradicts §5's tally of the same quantity. Provenance of the defect: the clause was appended in commit 8c574fca8 ('Those are counts of the four records / adjudicated here, not of the registry') to a numerator sentence that already read 'Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits' — the 4 was typed from the adjudication artifact's summary rather than derived from the records the sentence counts.
blockers.fix: Derive the number instead of typing it. Five records carry an admit/refuse verdict in this paper: NCT05918640 and NCT06571734 admit and treat, NCT04151342 admits observationally, NCT06094101 and NCT07188532 refuse. Either (a) make §3 read 'Those are counts of the five records this paper adjudicates, not of the registry' and make §5 read 'Five records were adjudicated: three admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse', or (b) keep both numbers but scope them explicitly — §3: 'Those are counts of the three records in this table that were adjudicated' and §5: 'Of the four candidates the screens flagged and the 2026-08-09 read adjudicated, one admits and treats, one admits observationally, and two refuse; NCT05918640 was confirmed in the 2026-08-07 read.' Do not leave two bare 'four's with different numerators.

blockers.summary: ARITH-B2 — §7 Data availability names three URL manifests where the sweep artifact records FOUR, and two of the three paths as written do not exist at this commit.
blockers.evidence: §7 (lines 243-245): 'The URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep are `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json`, `-c3.json` and `-c4.json`.' (1) The shorthand appended to that stem yields research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets-c3.json and -targets-c4.json, which do not exist at 78d345d3 and have never existed (`git log --all --diff-filter=A` finds no add). The real files are research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json and research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json. (2) research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> retrieval.runs is a FOUR-element list, and its targets_file values are: 'research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json', 'research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json', 'research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json', 'research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json'. The unnamed fourth manifest is not incidental: it carries `ct_sarcoma_2026_new` (verified present in that file), which is the unfielded sarcoma screen §2 relies on twice — 'one sarcoma screen was unfielded and did carry it' and 'the third [of the nine] inside the unfielded screen' (NCT06988475, whose retrieved_from.slug is 'ct-reverify-frontier-2026-08-07') — and it is where NCT04094610, one of the twelve lost records, was damaged.
blockers.fix: Replace the sentence with the four paths read off retrieval.runs: 'The URL manifests behind the 2026-08-07 sweep are `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json`, `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json`, `research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c4.json` and `research/manuscripts/modality-census/lit-targets-frontier-capability-2026-08-07.json`, the last of which carries the unfielded sarcoma screen.' Write each stem out in full rather than as a suffix.

p1s.summary: ARITH-P1-01 — nothing reads a single number in this paper, and the repository's own census says so. Every quantity I re-derived is correct at this commit and every one of them would survive an ordinary edit silently.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json -> papers['research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md'] = {"sentences": 87, "covered": 0, "with_a_number": 20, "with_a_number_covered": 0, "uncovered": 87, "uncovered_with_a_number": 20}; named_by for the same key is only 'systems/graph/publications.json'. No guard module reads the document. I re-derived and confirmed, at the pin: 400/199/526 screen sizes and 1,159 unique studies (fet-fusion-...-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.instruments[0..2].returns and retrieval.unique_studies_indexed); the fusion screen's saturation (its manifest URL carries pageSize=400 and it returned 400, while basket 199/400 and sarcoma 526/1000 did not saturate); NCT06571734 target enrolment 73 and NCT04151342 target enrolment 5500; NCT06571734's seven conditions on 2026-08-09 against ten on 2026-08-07 (the three dropped are 'Ewing Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma of Bone'); nine = one master screening protocol + seven DETERMINE arms (one NOT_YET_RECRUITING, NCT07440290) + one separate basket; eligibility text retrieved for three of those nine, two by per-NCT URL (ct_determine_arms, ct_nct03767075_bob) and the third inside the unfielded screen (ct_sarcoma_2026_new); NCT05918640's four listed conditions (three sarcomas + Pediatric Cancer), minimum age 10 Years, sponsor Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, one removal marker with verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean true; NCT06239272's 42 listed conditions with 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma' among them and the verbatim '1-30 years at the time of the biopsy'; twelve lost records (the union of transport_integrity.silently_damaged_records and unparseable_records is exactly 12 unique NCT ids), five recovered elsewhere in the same file (NCT05836571, NCT07695311, NCT07188532, NCT05275426, NCT06094101), three of the remaining seven from the two diagnosis condition searches (NCT00720174 COMPLETED, NCT05355753 TERMINATED, NCT01189253 TERMINATED per research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json); the NR4A3 term search's five studies and their conditions; NCT03767075's status_verified_date '2024-04'; five non-US endpoints with one HTTP 200 (ISRCTN), two 403 (EU CTIS, ANZCTR), one SSL handshake failure (jRCT) and one 404 from a wrong URL (WHO ICTRP); and the ISRCTN chondrosarcoma query's total_count 2. Not one of these is bound to its artifact by any instrument.
p1s.fix: Bind at least the load-bearing quantities the way S46-EIGHT-QUANTITIES-BOUND.md bound the ASO paper's: a guard module that reads the expected values AT RUN TIME from fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json (instruments[*].returns, retrieval.unique_studies_indexed, the lengths of confirmed_fusion_family_defined / molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined / candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification, the NR4A3 studies list length, NCT06571734's ten conditions) and from emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json (summary.* and the per-record listed_conditions / estimated_enrollment), then prove each binding by ablation with research/manuscripts/claim_ablation.py. The adjudication tally is the first one to bind: it is the quantity ARITH-B1 just got wrong, and nothing would have caught it.

p2s.summary: ARITH-P2-01 — §4.1 says one query ran at ISRCTN; the artifact records two, and the second query's single hit is never reported.
p2s.evidence: §4.1: 'the query that ran there was the parent term *chondrosarcoma*, and it returns two trials'. research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json -> endpoints[0] = {"registry": "ISRCTN (UK)", "result": "HTTP 200", "read": true, "queries": ["chondrosarcoma", "sarcoma AND fusion"]}, and isrctn_what_it_holds carries two blocks: query_chondrosarcoma (total_count 2) and query_sarcoma_and_fusion (total_count 1, ISRCTN52235823, a nanopore methylome-classification diagnostic study). The definite singular understates the search that was actually run — conservative for the absence claim, but wrong as stated, and it drops the one record in that registry the artifact calls 'the most relevant record the sweep returned'.

p2s.summary: ARITH-P2-02 — the abstract attaches the saturation to 'the screens that found them', but neither admitting trial is recorded as having come from the saturated screen.
p2s.evidence: Abstract: 'the screens that found them match keywords and one of them saturated, so two is a floor.' In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT06571734's retrieved_from.payload is 'ct_sarcoma_recruiting_fixed' (526 returned against pageSize=1000 — not saturated) and NCT05918640's is 'ct_nct05918640_lurbi_fet', a per-NCT URL rather than a screen at all. The saturated screen is ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed (400 against pageSize=400). The floor conclusion is sound and §5 states it exactly — 'Candidates entered the pool through keyword screens ... and the fusion screen came back at its page limit, so it is truncated' — so the fix is to make the abstract say the pool saturated, not the screens that found these two.

p2s.summary: ARITH-P2-03 — §7 credits both un-URL'd artifacts with naming an API base; one of them names no URL at all.
p2s.evidence: §7: 'the other two ran from inline manifests that were never committed, and name the API base only.' True of emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json, whose retrieval block carries "api": "ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies)". Not true of non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json, whose _retrieval block is {route, actions_run_id, slug, date_et} and contains no endpoint URL or API base anywhere in the file — the endpoints are identified by registry name only.

p2s.summary: ARITH-P2-04 — the front-matter scope enumerates three unread non-US endpoints where there are four.
p2s.evidence: Front matter: 'Two further non-US registries refused automated access and a third failed at the TLS handshake; all three are reported as unread endpoints rather than as absences.' non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json -> endpoints lists five non-US endpoints, of which FOUR were unread: EU CTIS (403), ANZCTR (403), jRCT (SSL handshake failure) and WHO ICTRP (HTTP 404, "THE URL WAS A GUESS AND IT WAS WRONG ... ICTRP remains genuinely uncovered"). The abstract and §5 both carry the fourth; the scope block does not, so the paper's own metadata understates the uncovered surface by one endpoint.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: 1,159 does not equal 400+199+526 — the paper never claims the parts sum to it; 1,159 is retrieval.unique_studies_indexed, a dedup total across all instruments including the term searches and the condition searches, and it is printed as an indexed total rather than as a sum.
Five NR4A3 studies but only four kinds named in the parenthetical — two of the five (NCT02968888, NCT03033953) are both exercise-physiology studies, so the list is a list of kinds and is complete.
NCT06571734's condition list disagrees between the two artifacts (ten vs seven) — the paper prints both, dates both, and calls the difference unexplained rather than silently picking one.

The 400 might be a coincidence rather than a page limit — the manifest URL ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed carries pageSize=400 and the screen returned 400, so 'its page limit' is exact; basket (199/400) and sarcoma (526/1000) are correctly not called saturated.

NCT06239272's age bound might be the registry's fielded maximum_age of '30 Years' misread as a range — the paper takes 1-30 from the verbatim criterion 'Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS' and says explicitly that it is measured at biopsy rather than at enrolment, which is exactly what the record states.

Twelve lost records looked unreconcilable at first (18 record-instances, 13 unparseable entries) — it is the union of unique NCT ids across both failure modes, which is exactly 12, and the five recoverable ones are exactly the five that reappear elsewhere in the same file.

The quoted FET criterion for NCT05918640 could be transport-damaged, since the record carries a removal marker — the paper says so in §2 and the artifact carries verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean: true for that sentence.
notes: I re-derived every printed number in the paper from the committed artifact that produces it, at the pin. Twenty-odd quantities check out exactly — the three screen sizes and their page limits, 1,159 indexed, the 12/5/7/3 transport arithmetic (which is subtle and right: twelve is the union of unique NCT ids across two failure modes), the nine records decomposing as 1 master + 7 arms + 1 basket with exactly one not-yet-recruiting, three-of-nine with eligibility text and which route each came by, 73 and 5500 target enrolments, seven-vs-ten conditions, 42 conditions and the verbatim 1-30-at-biopsy bound, five NR4A3 studies, five non-US endpoints, two ISRCTN trials, April 2024, age 10, Canadian sites. Two numbers do not: the adjudication denominator, which the paper prints as 'four' in two places with two different numerators and which is five records paper-wide (ARITH-B1), and the data-availability manifest list, which names three of four and misspells two stems (ARITH-B2). Both are the same failure mode — a total typed from an artifact's summary block rather than derived from the records the sentence actually counts. The deeper reservation is ARITH-P1-01: research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json records 0 of 20 numeric sentences covered for this document, so every one of the numbers I checked by hand is unguarded, and ARITH-B1 is what that gap costs. The central claim itself is carried — NCT05918640's FET-family criterion and NCT06571734's translocation cohort are both in the artifacts with emc_in_listed_conditions false, and both refusals are recorded with their verbatim restricting criteria. Process note: a repository-wide grep for 'candidates_adjudicated' incidentally printed one line from research/autonomy/hardening-state/PUB-STRATEGY-ARCH.json in its output; I did not open that file and no finding here derives from it — ARITH-B1 was derived from the manuscript and the two literature artifacts before that grep ran.
